identity.description: Bottom-up hierarchical clusterer: starts with every row as its own cluster and greedily merges the closest pair under a linkage criterion (ward/complete/average/single), producing a full merge tree — the dendrogram — that can be cut at ANY height, so the segment count is a post-fit choice rather than a pre-fit commitment. Like DBSCAN it has no native predict() for unseen rows (fit_predict only) — new-point assignment is a wrapper responsibility. interpretabilityClass 'Rules' is the nearest 4-way fit for the dendrogram: a human-readable nested merge structure, though not literal decision rules.

emits.note: labels for the chosen cut (n_clusters or distance_threshold); the REAL fitted knowledge is the merge tree (children_ + distances_) for which no paramsAsOutput enum value exists — see portTypeProposals

portTypeProposals.name: linkage-tree
portTypeProposals.why: the dendrogram (children_ + merge distances) is this model's distinguishing artifact — a per-model structure downstream components could consume for multi-resolution cuts, taxonomy displays, and cophenetic analysis; today it has no port NOR a paramsAsOutput enum value, so it rides only in the driver notes

n_clusters.note: a CUT of the tree, not a fit parameter — sweepable by silhouette across cut heights without refitting conceptually; mutually exclusive with distance_threshold

metric.note: ward REQUIRES euclidean — any other pairing is invalid input

compute_distances.note: must be true to export the dendrogram

invariances.why: every merge decision compares metric distances (Euclidean under ward) — an unscaled high-variance feature dictates the entire merge order and thus the whole tree
feature-level monotone maps change pairwise distances nonlinearly, reordering merges; (single/complete linkage are invariant to monotone maps of the DISTANCES, but not of the features)
pairwise distances are undefined on missing coordinates — the distance matrix cannot be formed
merges need a metric space; encoded categoricals distort it (though a precomputed-distance mode exists for genuinely custom metrics, it is outside this driver's default path)
no likelihood and no global objective — but note the per-linkage biases: ward shares k-means' compact-spherical preference, single linkage chains, complete linkage favors equal diameters
the algorithm materializes O(n²) pairwise structure — memory and time make ~10⁴-10⁵ rows the practical ceiling, a mechanism-level bound, not a tuning issue
there is no decision function for unseen rows at all — the fit is a tree over the training set

featureStats.why: the O(n²) pairwise cost makes raw sample count itself the gating statistic — beyond ~10⁴-10⁵ rows this family member is mechanically excluded and routed to k-means
merge order is a pure function of distances; large variance spread means the tree encodes one feature's units, mandating the scale placement
cluster tendency check — a dendrogram is ALWAYS produced, even on uniform noise, so tendency must be established before any cut is read as structure

modelMetrics.why: the hierarchical-specific fit measure: how faithfully the tree's merge heights preserve the original pairwise distances — a low value means the dendrogram is a distortion, whatever the silhouette says
the cut (segment count) is a post-fit choice; sweeping silhouette across cut heights is how it is chosen and defended — the family's validation axis, not holdout AUC
resample-and-recut agreement separates real hierarchy from merge-order artifacts — the unsupervised stand-in for a holdout
a large jump between successive merge distances marks a natural cut height; its absence warns that any chosen k is arbitrary

edgeCases.behavior: O(n²) distance structure exhausts memory before any result
chaining — thin bridges of points merge distinct clusters into one serpent
sklearn raises — the two cut rules are mutually exclusive
no native predict() — refitting with appended rows rebuilds a different tree and silently relabels everything
merge order (and thus the tree) depends on tie-breaking; rare with continuous features, common with encoded/discrete ones

driver.wrapperNeeds: REQUIRED for the score path: fit_predict only — the wrapper assigns NEW rows by nearest fitted-cluster centroid (computed and persisted at fit time) or kNN over the labeled training rows; dendrogram export additionally needs compute_distances=True plus a children_/distances_ → scipy linkage-matrix conversion
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded fit; fitted labels/tree are read-only thereafter

canBeSeeds.via: cluster-id (re-cut at multiple heights from one fit)

placementClaims.why: the pairwise distance matrix cannot be formed with missing coordinates
symmetrizing heavy tails changes distances toward the compact-cluster geometry ward assumes; it also reduces spurious chaining under single linkage
distance-based by mechanism — an unscaled feature's units become the tree's topology
a metric space over numeric vectors is a precondition; discrete encodings also multiply tied merge distances (see edge case), so heavy-categorical inputs deserve a bank-entry caution
